title: Normativity Structure Analysis Schema
description: Structured analysis of normative claims in philosophical texts. Maps the structure, type, source, and bindingness of normative prescriptions, and diagnoses the overall normative architecture.

analysis_id.description: Unique identifier for this normativity analysis run

normative_claims.description: Identified normative claims in the text

claim_text.description: Full text of the normative claim

ought_type.description: Type of normativity expressed by the claim

categorical_or_hypothetical.description: Whether the claim is categorical (binding regardless of desires), hypothetical (conditional on desires or goals), or both

source_of_normativity.description: Account of where the normativity originates

reasons_internalism.description: Whether reasons for this claim are internal to the agent's motivational set, external, or mixed

bindingness_mechanism.description: Account of how or why this normative claim binds agents

motivation_justification_distinction.description: Distinction between motivating and justifying reasons for this claim

motivating_reason.description: The motivating reason — what actually moves the agent

justifying_reason.description: The justifying reason — what rationally supports the claim

gap.description: Whether a gap exists between motivating and justifying reasons, and its nature

normative_architecture.description: Overall architecture of the normative system in the text

foundational_principle.description: The foundational normative principle or principles identified

regress_assessment.description: Assessment of how the system handles normative regress (e.g., 'stops at fundamental principle', 'coherentist holism avoids regress', 'infinite regress unresolved')
